question: What is the core principle of 'Strict Liability' in anti-doping regulations?
options: The athlete is only responsible if intentional cheating can be proven in court
The athlete is solely responsible for any prohibited substance found in their sample
The coach and team doctor bear primary legal liability for positive tests
Liability only applies if the substance provided a measurable performance gain
explanation: Strict Liability means an athlete is fully accountable for any substance detected in their sample, whether ingested intentionally, accidentally, or through contaminated food or supplements.

question: What does the abbreviation 'TUE' stand for in sports integrity?
options: Total Urine Evaluation
Therapeutic Use Exemption
Timed Urgent Examination
Targeted Universal Enforcement
explanation: A Therapeutic Use Exemption (TUE) allows an athlete with an approved medical condition to use an otherwise prohibited medication under strict medical supervision.

question: Why are dietary supplements considered high-risk for competitive athletes?
options: They are always illegal to purchase in pharmacies
They lack mandatory pre-market approval and can contain undeclared prohibited ingredients
All dietary vitamins are banned under the WADA Code
They degrade protein synthesis in healthy muscles
explanation: Dietary supplements are regulated more like foods than pharmaceutical drugs in many countries, creating risks of cross-contamination or hidden designer stimulants.

question: Which of the following cold medication ingredients is prohibited in-competition above a specific urinary threshold?
options: Paracetamol / Acetaminophen
Pseudoephedrine
Vitamin C (Ascorbic Acid)
Saline nasal rinse
explanation: Pseudoephedrine is prohibited In-Competition when urinary concentration exceeds 150 µg/mL. Athletes are advised to stop taking it 24 hours prior to competition.

question: Which independent certification logo indicates rigorous third-party batch testing for banned substances?
options: Informed Sport / NSF Certified for Sport
100% Herbal Guaranteed
Doctor Recommended Online
Fast Gains Laboratory Tested
explanation: Informed Sport, BSCG, and NSF Certified for Sport test specific manufacturing batches for substances on the WADA Prohibited List.

question: What is the status of pure Creatine Monohydrate on the WADA Prohibited List?
options: Prohibited at all times
Prohibited only in-competition
Not prohibited (permitted)
Prohibited only for athletes under 18
explanation: Pure creatine monohydrate is NOT prohibited by WADA or national anti-doping organizations. However, athletes should ensure it is tested for cross-contamination.

question: Which class of substances on the WADA List is prohibited at ALL TIMES (both in and out of competition)?
options: Anabolic Androgenic Steroids (S1)
Cannabinoids (S8)
Narcotics (S7)
Alcohol
explanation: Anabolic agents (S1), Peptide hormones (S2), Beta-2 agonists (S3, with specific inhaled limits), and Hormone modulators (S4) are prohibited at all times.

question: How long does a standard in-competition period typically begin under WADA rules?
options: At 11:59 PM on the day before a competition through the end of the sample collection
Exactly 30 days before the competition date
Only when the whistle blows to start the event
One week before the athletes travel
explanation: Unless approved otherwise for a specific sport, the In-Competition period begins at 11:59 p.m. on the day before a competition in which the athlete is scheduled to participate.

question: If a friend at your fitness gym offers you an unlabelled powder claiming 'crazy pumps without side effects', what should you do?
options: Try a half-scoop to see how your body reacts
Politely decline and only consume verified, third-party certified products
Take it only on heavy leg training days
Mix it with water so it dilutes any prohibited elements
explanation: Never consume unlabelled or open supplements. Diluting an illegal substance or taking smaller quantities still results in positive analytical findings and health risks.

question: What is the global organization responsible for harmonizing anti-doping policies across sports?
options: WADA (World Anti-Doping Agency)
FIFA Medical Commission
Interpol Sports Division
WHO Doping Taskforce
explanation: WADA (World Anti-Doping Agency), established in 1999, oversees the World Anti-Doping Code and collaborates with National Anti-Doping Agencies (like NADA) globally.

question: Why does WADA strictly regulate intravenous (IV) infusions or injections?
options: IV needles are painful for athletes
IV infusions over 100 mL per 12 hours can mask banned substances or artificially manipulate blood parameters
All hydration must come exclusively from food
They are only banned in water sports
explanation: Intravenous infusions exceeding 100 mL per 12-hour period are prohibited (M2. Chemical and Physical Manipulation) unless legitimately received in hospital treatments.

question: Can a product marketed as '100% Herbal & All-Natural' cause a positive doping test?
options: No, herbal ingredients are always completely exempted from anti-doping tests
Yes, natural herbs can contain prohibited alkaloids (e.g., ephedra) or undeclared synthetic compounds
Only if taken together with dairy milk
Only during winter sporting events
explanation: Plants contain potent pharmacological compounds (like ephedrine from ma huang), and herbal products are notorious for synthetic adulteration.

question: What is an 'Adverse Analytical Finding' (AAF)?
options: A report from a WADA-accredited laboratory identifying the presence of a prohibited substance in a sample
A failed psychological questionnaire by a player
A blood test indicating dehydration only
An athlete missing a scheduled training session
explanation: An AAF is the official laboratory term for when an athlete's urine or blood sample contains a prohibited substance, its metabolites, or markers.

question: What should an athlete do BEFORE taking a new prescription medicine given by their family doctor?
options: Inform the doctor that they are a tested athlete, and verify the active ingredient against Global DRO or NADA guidelines
Take it immediately and keep the receipt
Only check if the medicine comes in red pills
Ask a teammate on WhatsApp
explanation: Athletes must notify their healthcare providers of their anti-doping obligations and verify every active ingredient before ingestion.

question: What is the primary danger of using Selective Androgen Receptor Modulators (SARMs) like Ostarine?
options: They cause instant loss of appetite
They are unapproved experimental drugs with proven risks of liver toxicity, cardiovascular strain, and immediate bans
They turn urine a bright blue color
They only affect non-athletes
explanation: SARMs have never received regulatory approval for general human use and are strictly prohibited under WADA S1.2 due to severe organ toxicity risks.

question: Is caffeine currently on the WADA Prohibited List?
options: Yes, all caffeine is banned
No, caffeine is on the WADA Monitoring Program, meaning it is permitted but monitored for misuse patterns
It is only banned in chess competitions
It is banned if consumed before 9 AM
explanation: Caffeine was removed from the Prohibited List in 2004. It remains on the Monitoring Program so WADA can track overall usage trends.

question: What does 'Whereabouts' information refer to for testing pool athletes?
options: Providing their detailed daily location and a 60-minute daily testing window to enable unannounced out-of-competition testing
Sharing their live GPS location with social media followers
The location of their favorite gym only
Their travel receipts from vacation flights
explanation: Whereabouts requirements allow anti-doping organizations to conduct unannounced testing 365 days a year without giving prior notice to athletes.

question: What happens if an athlete misses three Whereabouts tests or filing deadlines in a 12-month window?
options: They receive a polite warning letter only
It constitutes an Anti-Doping Rule Violation (ADRV) resulting in a potential 1 to 2-year suspension
They must pay a $50 fine
Their coach is suspended instead
explanation: Any combination of three missed tests or filing failures within a rolling 12-month period constitutes an ADRV under Code Article 2.4.

question: If an athlete has asthma and uses an approved salbutamol inhaler, what rule applies?
options: Inhaled salbutamol is permitted within maximum daily therapeutic limits (up to 1600 mcg/24h); exceeding this requires a TUE
All asthma inhalers are completely illegal for runners
They can take unlimited doses without any restriction
They can use oral salbutamol tablets without a prescription
explanation: Inhaled salbutamol is permitted up to 1600 mcg over 24 hours (not exceeding 600 mcg over 8 hours). Oral salbutamol is strictly prohibited.

question: What is the single most sustainable foundation for athletic recovery and clean performance?
options: Taking 10 different test boosters every morning
Prioritizing 7-9 hours of regular sleep, whole food nutrition, adequate hydration, and structured training cycles
Skipping rest days to train twice as much as competitors
Relying on unregulated online proprietary blends
explanation: Sleep, whole nutrition, hydration, and progressive overload produce 95%+ of athletic adaptations safely and sustainably.
